The records: which record controls title, and what gets booked

Start with a case

  • JPM Coin: a bank deposit token
  • BUIDL: which ownership record governs?
  • Ripple and Securitize: money and securities roles
  • Securitize: compare four ownership record models
  • USDC: creation, transfer and redemption
  • DTC: securities ownership through an intermediary
  • Subscribe to a fund: follow the steps
  • Debits and credits: the full teaching guide

Each link opens the named record directly. The complete reference overview continues below; a shared transaction does not merge money, fund ownership or intermediary records.

This page follows the record, not the token: who books what, and whose record decides who owns it. It opens with the 3 process walks of how a trade, a payment and a fund subscription work today, and the debit-and-credit entries each party books at every step; then the steps-and-rights walks and transaction maps; the 17 asset traces (USDC from mint to redemption, BUIDL and others); the 7 accounting layers; the current U.S. stack; Securitize's 4 record models; DTC's records; the SEC transfer agent proposal; and 61 dated tokenization and clearing filings. A token, a chain or a software vendor books nothing by itself; only an entity whose own books hold the asset or the claim does.

    Step 1: Open the account

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    A brokerage account is a relationship. Nobody has booked the security yet.
    Seats
    • Seat: Investor · Today: Unnamed teaching customer · Overlap: A wallet is not this account · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Carrying broker · Today: Unnamed. LST on the NSCC directory only means the firm processes listed equity through NSCC — not that it is this trade’s broker. · Overlap: — · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 2: Trade date

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    Buyer and seller (through brokers) take on obligations. The issuer and Cede do not move.
    Seats
    • Seat: Investor · Today: Books a securities entitlement against the broker · Overlap: — · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Carrying broker · Today: Customer receivable / payable to the street · Overlap: — · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Venue · Today: Example: NYSE LLC. Trade may be internalized or another exchange. No $10,000 books of this trade. · Overlap: Securitize Markets is a different venue family · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Issuer / Cede · Today: No entry. Cede is already the registered holder. · Overlap: Token does not rewrite the issuer register · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 3: Clear

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    NSCC novates. One long or short per member per security versus NSCC as CCP.
    Seats
    • Seat: CCP · Today: National Securities Clearing Corporation (Rule 11 CNS) · Overlap: A token does not book NSCC’s receivable/payable pair · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Clearing member · Today: Full-service NSCC Member. Directory “CNS” is a muni preference, not this seat. LST = listed equity through NSCC. Examples (not this trade): BofA Securities; Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC has LST without the muni-CNS flag. · Overlap: Hidden Road is a DTC/FICC member — a different utility · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 4: Settle — securities and cash

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    DTC’s participant file moves the security. Cash is not paid trade-by-trade: NSCC nets, DTC submits NSS, the Fed debits settling banks.
    Seats
    • Seat: CSD / participant file · Today: The Depository Trust Company · Overlap: DTC tokenization can re-represent the participant entitlement. First phase is free of value. · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Nominee · Today: Cede & Co. still on the issuer register · Overlap: Saved design keeps Cede as registered holder · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Transfer agent · Today: Idle. Example: Computershare (2015 TA-1). If this register turned, it would be direct registration — a different process. · Overlap: Securitize is the BUIDL TA, not this equity’s TA · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Settlement agent · Today: DTC submits the NSS file for NSCC · Overlap: — · Overtake: No
    • Seat: NSS / Reserve Banks · Today: Federal Reserve Banks debit/credit settling-bank Fed accounts · Overlap: No chain confirmation is this credit · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Settling bank · Today: Member-designated. 47 banks on the 31 Aug 2026 public list (examples: JPM, BofA). List is eligibility, not this trade’s bank. · Overlap: Hidden Road is not this cash bank · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 5: Hold — three records of the same security

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    Customer file at the broker, participant file at DTC, Cede on the issuer register.
    Seats
    • Seat: Beneficial owner · Today: Investor’s entitlement vs the broker · Overlap: Wallet control is not this tier · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Participant record · Today: DTC file · Overlap: Token may reclass how DTC records the position · Overtake: No — same entitlement, different wrapper
    • Seat: Registered holder · Today: Cede & Co. · Overlap: Cede stays named · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 6: Service, exit, or fail

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    What
    A fail stays on the CCP/member/settling-bank waterfall. Issuer and wallet do not absorb it by default.
    Seats
    Seat: CCP on a fail · Today: NSCC receivable from the failing member remains · Overlap: — · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 1: Identify the claim

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    The payer holds a bank deposit. That is a different claim from USDC.
    Seats
    • Seat: Payer’s money · Today: Deposit at the sending bank · Overlap: USDC is Circle’s liability, not this deposit · Overtake: No — different claim
    • Seat: Distributor · Today: — · Overlap: Coinbase has USDC distribution economics. Not the issuer. · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 2: Authorize the order

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    Accepted payment order is still memo until funded and processed.
    Seats
    • Seat: Sending bank · Today: Unnamed teaching bank. Example only: Payward Financial / Kraken Financial — Fedwire Funds only, use unproven. · Overlap: A wallet signature is not Bank A’s debit · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Reserve Bank service · Today: Federal Reserve Banks (OC 6 / Reg J) · Overlap: Idle until a dollar payout actually runs · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 3: Fund the sending bank

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    A message does not supply reserves.
    Seats
    Seat: Sending bank · Today: Must have spendable funds. Kraken’s example account has no intraday credit. · Overlap: USDC mint moves Circle’s reserve assets, not this bank’s Fed account — and only on mint/redeem, not a holder transfer · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 4: The service transfer

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    Fedwire always moves Bank A, the Fed, and Bank B. A USDC holder-to-holder transfer need not touch any of those books.
    Seats
    • Seat: Sending bank · Today: Dr customer deposit / Cr reserve at Fed · Overlap: Idle on a token transfer · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Reserve Banks · Today: Dr liability to Bank A / Cr liability to Bank B · Overlap: No entry on a USDC holder transfer · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Receiving bank · Today: Dr reserve / Cr beneficiary deposit · Overlap: Idle unless a separate off-ramp · Overtake: No
    • Seat: USDC issuer · Today: — (not in this process) · Overlap: Circle Internet Financial, LLC still owes outstanding USDC; no entry on holder transfer · Overtake: No — never had this Fedwire seat
    • Seat: Messaging · Today: — · Overlap: SWIFT may coordinate a commitment. No $1m proprietary entry. · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 5: What the recipient received

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    The receiving bank now owes the beneficiary a deposit. The payer’s invoice is a separate commercial entry.
    Seats
    Seat: Beneficiary · Today: Deposit at Bank B · Overlap: USDC holder has an issuer claim, not automatically a direct redemption right · Overtake: No — different claim
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 6: Exception or redeem

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    What
    Fedwire exception stays on bank/Fed books. USDC exit is inverse of mint, then this process for the dollar payout.
    Seats
    • Seat: USDC issuer · Today: — · Overlap: Circle Dr USDC liability / Cr reserve cash · Overtake: No — this is a different instrument leaving, then Fedwire
    • Seat: Reserve owner · Today: — · Overlap: Circle Reserve Fund (~88% of year-end 2025 USDC reserves) · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Reserve manager · Today: — · Overlap: BlackRock Advisors, LLC (Circle fund only — not BUIDL’s IM) · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Reserve custodian · Today: — · Overlap: BNY for the Circle Reserve Fund. Separate from BUIDL custody and RLUSD custody. · Overtake: No
    • Seat: Payout bank · Today: Then Process C (Fedwire) again · Overlap: Unnamed. Do not assume Kraken, BNY, or Circle National Trust. · Overtake: No
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    The four kinds of books

    · 4 rows

    If this entity’s proprietary books do not debit or credit the economic object, they are not the issuer, holder, CCP, cash settler or reserve owner. A fiduciary file can still be a real role. Transport, software and an unused issuer register have no entry.

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/books_hub.json

    Proprietary books

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?

    Step 3: Clear — CCP becomes the counterparty

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Tokenized trade books
    Question
    Who books receivables and payables as principal to both members?
    Role test
    That principal pair is the CCP. The member who has the CCP receivable/payable is the clearing member. The firm who has the customer receivable/payable is the carrying broker. They can be one legal person or two — the entries say.
    Entries
    • Entity label: CCP (CNS) · Occupant: National Securities Clearing Corporation · Process office: Yes · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Receivable from selling member · Credit: Payable to buying member · Role performed: Central counterparty · Note: Matching without NSCC principal receivables/payables is not clearing. Which member sits across from NSCC stays unnamed. · Occupant status: verified · Occupant boundary: CNS is an NSCC service. This names the CCP office, not a particular clearing member.

    • Entity label: Payer · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: memo · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Instruction principal · Note: Authorization is not payment.
    • Entity label: Sending bank · Occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial · Process office: No · Book kind: memo · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Instruction agent — may reject · Note: Example occupant only. The teaching payer’s bank remains unidentified. · Occupant status: example · Occupant boundary: Wyoming SPDI with a limited-purpose Kansas City Fed account: Fedwire Funds only; no intraday/discount-window credit; no services for the Kraken exchange or other Payward entities; actual payment use unproven. Example of a crypto-native sending bank, not Bank A in this teaching $1,000,000 payment.
    • Entity label: Reserve Bank service · Occupant: Federal Reserve Banks · Process office: Yes · Book kind: memo · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Service operator — not yet rebooking reserves · Note: Taught office is the Federal Reserve Banks. · Occupant status: verified · Occupant boundary: Fedwire Funds is a Reserve Bank service under OC 6 and Regulation J Subpart B. This names the cash-settlement operator, not a particular sending or receiving bank and not a master-account grant.
    Overlay entries
    Entity label: Chain / wallet software · Occupant: Circle Technology Services, LLC / Arc Network Services LLC · Process office: No · Book kind: none · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Transport — no $1,000,000 proprietary entry · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: Software/network vendors. No $1,000,000 proprietary USDC or reserve entry. Not the issuer and not Fedwire.
    Sources: Process debits, credits and roles — teaching T-accounts (Read the full saved research: Process debits, credits, and roles; research notes) (2026-09-10) · Federal Reserve Operating Circular 6 and Regulation J Fedwire Funds route

    Step 3: Provide sending-bank resources

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Tokenized trade books
    Question
    Did the sending bank have spendable funds, or only a message?
    Role test
    A payment message does not supply reserves. Prefunding, overdraft and available balance are different entries.
    Entries
    Entity label: Sending bank · Occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: — (or Dr due from customer if not already collected) · Credit: Reserve or available settlement balance remains until C4 · Role performed: Sending participant — must be funded · Note: Even this example does not prove funded use. Unlimited credit is expressly not granted. · Occupant status: example · Occupant boundary: Wyoming SPDI with a limited-purpose Kansas City Fed account: Fedwire Funds only; no intraday/discount-window credit; no services for the Kraken exchange or other Payward entities; actual payment use unproven. Example of a crypto-native sending bank, not Bank A in this teaching $1,000,000 payment.
    Overlay entries
    Entity label: USDC reserve owner · Occupant: Circle Reserve Fund (Rule 2a-7 vehicle) · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Reserve assets (if this is a mint, not a holder transfer) · Credit: Cash (if reserves are being invested) · Role performed: Reserve owner — only on mint/redeem, not on a holder-to-holder transfer · Note: Manager and custodian are not this row. · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: Reserve-owner books only on mint/redeem, not on a holder-to-holder transfer.
    Sources: Process debits, credits and roles — teaching T-accounts (Read the full saved research: Process debits, credits, and roles; research notes) (2026-09-10) · Federal Reserve Operating Circular 6 and Regulation J Fedwire Funds route

    Step 4: Complete the service transfer

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Tokenized trade books
    Question
    Whose liabilities to the two banks just rebooked?
    Role test
    Fedwire always moves sending bank, Reserve Banks, and receiving bank. A USDC holder-to-holder transfer need not touch any of those books.
    Entries
    • Entity label: Payer · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Payable / expense · Credit: Deposit at sending bank · Role performed: Holder spending the deposit claim
    • Entity label: Sending bank · Occupant: Payward Financial, Inc. d/b/a Kraken Financial · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Customer-deposit liability · Credit: Reserve balance at the Fed · Role performed: Sending participant / obligor of the payer’s money · Note: If this entity were Bank A, its reserve account would move. It is not asserted to be Bank A here. · Occupant status: example · Occupant boundary: Wyoming SPDI with a limited-purpose Kansas City Fed account: Fedwire Funds only; no intraday/discount-window credit; no services for the Kraken exchange or other Payward entities; actual payment use unproven. Example of a crypto-native sending bank, not Bank A in this teaching $1,000,000 payment.
    • Entity label: Reserve Banks · Occupant: Federal Reserve Banks · Process office: Yes · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Liability to sending bank (reserves) · Credit: Liability to receiving bank (reserves) · Role performed: Cash-settlement operator · Note: They rebook their own liabilities to the two banks. Fedwire-as-message is not a fourth $1,000,000 claim. · Occupant status: verified · Occupant boundary: Fedwire Funds is a Reserve Bank service under OC 6 and Regulation J Subpart B. This names the cash-settlement operator, not a particular sending or receiving bank and not a master-account grant.
    • Entity label: Receiving bank · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Reserve balance at the Fed · Credit: Customer-deposit liability · Role performed: Receiving participant / new obligor to the beneficiary · Note: Teaching receiving bank unnamed. A USDC recipient bank is a different seat on redemption payout.
    • Entity label: Messaging / coordination ledger · Occupant: SWIFT · Process office: No · Book kind: none · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Not the cash-settlement operator · Note: If it only coordinates a commitment, it has no $1,000,000 proprietary entry. See the saved SWIFT Saturday walkthrough. · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: If the ledger only coordinates a funded commitment, SWIFT has no $1,000,000 proprietary entry. Not the Reserve Banks and not Bank A/B.
    Overlay entries
    • Entity label: USDC holder A · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Receivable settled / purchase / gift (teaching) · Credit: USDC · Role performed: Holder exiting the token claim · Note: Holder-to-holder transfer.
    • Entity label: USDC holder B · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: USDC · Credit: Payable settled / sale / gift (teaching) · Role performed: Holder of the same issuer liability

Holding USDC is not automatic direct redemption. Not Circle National Trust and not Arc.

The Fed does not rebook reserves unless a separate dollar payout runs Process C.
    • Entity label: Commercial banks · Occupant: Commercial banks (idle on token transfer) · Process office: No · Book kind: none · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Idle unless a separate off-ramp runs Process C · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: Holder-to-holder USDC does not debit Bank A, credit Bank B, or rebook Fed reserves. Banks move again only if a separate redemption payout runs Process C.

    Step 5: What the recipient received

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Tokenized trade books
    Question
    Which bank now owes the beneficiary, and is the invoice a separate entry?
    Role test
    Receiving bank’s customer-deposit credit is the money the beneficiary holds. Discharge of the payer’s invoice is a commercial entry on payer/beneficiary books, not the Fedwire rule.
    Entries
    • Entity label: Beneficiary · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Deposit at receiving bank · Credit: Receivable / revenue · Role performed: Holder of the new deposit claim
    • Entity label: Receiving bank · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: — (reserves already at C4) · Credit: Customer-deposit liability (already credited at C4) · Role performed: Obligor of the beneficiary’s money · Note: Article 4-A-style teaching: acceptance creates the duty to pay the beneficiary.
    Overlay entries
    Entity label: USDC recipient · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: USDC · Credit: Receivable / revenue · Role performed: Holder of issuer liability — not automatically a direct redemption customer · Note: Holder-tier question remains.
    Sources: Process debits, credits and roles — teaching T-accounts (Read the full saved research: Process debits, credits, and roles; research notes) (2026-09-10) · Federal Reserve Operating Circular 6 and Regulation J Fedwire Funds route

    Step 6: Exception, return, or redeem

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: Tokenized trade books
    Question
    Is this an error on Process C, or a different asset exiting to dollars?
    Role test
    Fedwire exception stays on bank/Fed books. USDC redemption is inverse of mint, then Process C for the dollar payout. Burn without that bank credit is not payout.
    Entries
    Entity label: Sending or receiving bank (error) · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Correction / receivable as the rule provides · Credit: Customer deposit or reserve as the rule provides · Role performed: Exception handler under the transfer rules · Note: Teaching placeholder — not a named fail.
    Overlay entries
    • Entity label: USDC issuer · Occupant: Circle Internet Financial, LLC · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: USDC liability · Credit: Reserve cash · Role performed: Obligor redeeming · Note: Mint is the inverse: Dr reserve assets Cr USDC liability. · Occupant status: verified · Occupant boundary: Saved USDC terms: relevant non-EEA issuer. Holding USDC is not automatic direct redemption. Not Circle National Trust and not Arc.
    • Entity label: Reserve owner · Occupant: Circle Reserve Fund (Rule 2a-7 vehicle) · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Cash or due from issuer · Credit: Reserve assets (cash leaving) · Role performed: Reserve owner · Note: Whoever booked the matching assets. May be the issuer, a fund, or a trust — the entry says which. If issuer and owner are the same person, this is the same books as the issuer row. · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: Circle’s 2025 Form 10-K: about 88% of year-end USDC reserves in the Circle Reserve Fund, remainder generally cash in FBO-titled bank accounts. Fund ownership of reserve assets is not the issuer liability to token holders.
    • Entity label: Reserve manager · Occupant: BlackRock Advisors, LLC · Process office: No · Book kind: none · Debit: — · Credit: — · Role performed: Agency only · Note: Can change composition without taking ownership. · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: April 18, 2025 S-1/A: manager of Circle Reserve Fund investments and operations, subject to the fund board. Not BlackRock Financial Management, Inc. (BUIDL) and not the BlackRock parent. Not the reserve owner and not the custodian.
    • Entity label: Reserve custodian · Occupant: The Bank of New York Mellon · Process office: No · Book kind: fiduciary · Debit: Release of safekeeping obligation · Credit: Safekeeping inventory down · Role performed: Custodian — not the obligor to token holders · Occupant status: dated · Occupant boundary: Circle 2025 annual report/10-K: Circle Reserve Fund assets custodied by BNY. Brand as published. Separate from BUIDL fund custody and from RLUSD reserve custody. Not the USDC issuer.
    • Entity label: Payout bank (then Process C) · Occupant: unnamed · Process office: No · Book kind: proprietary · Debit: Issuer or fund cash · Credit: Reserves / due to beneficiary bank · Role performed: Payment-services / conversion — then sending bank on Process C · Note: After Circle Dr USDC liability Cr reserve cash, payout is an ordinary Process C sending bank. Occupant unnamed; do not assume Kraken Financial, BNY, or Circle National Trust.

    Steps and rights: Buy a broker-held security

    · 7 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/TOKENIZATION_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY_2026-09-01.json › steps_rights_hub.routes

    Buy a broker-held security

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Baseline
    A secondary-market purchase routed through NSCC CNS and DTC
    Overlay
    DTC tokenized entitlements
    Scope
    An eligible U.S. broker-to-broker cash-security trade. Not every security or trade uses CNS; direct registration, primary issuance, Treasuries and derivatives have different routes. Customer, clearing-member and depository records are separate.
    Clock
    Current conventional service model; crypto comparison uses the December 11, 2025 conditional no-action architecture. The letter is not a production receipt or Commission approval.
    Chain
    • Investor ↔ broker: customer account
    • Clearing member ↔ NSCC: accepted CNS obligations
    • Participant ↔ DTC: security entitlement
    • Cede ↔ issuer / transfer agent: registered holding
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 1: Open the right accountDependency

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    The investor establishes a brokerage account and chooses how the security will be held.
    Actors
    Investor; broker; carrying or clearing firm.
    Right
    Account rights and an instruction relationship exist. Opening an account does not itself acquire a security.
    Record
    Customer agreement and account registration.
    Proof
    Identify the carrying entity, holding method and permitted activity.
    Crypto
    The reviewed DTC design adds participant-linked registered wallets; it does not give any wallet owner direct DTC membership.
    Status
    dependency
    Gap
    Access remains institution-controlled.
    Needed
    For a named user, recover the broker-to-participant and wallet authorization chain.
    Sources: SEC / FINRA: how securities are held (2023-07-12) · DTC tokenization no-action letter (2025-12-11)

    Step 2: Execute and confirm the tradeUnproven

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    The broker obtains execution; trade details establish the agreed security, quantity, price and settlement terms.
    Actors
    Buyer and seller through brokers; trading venue where used.
    Right
    A trade obligation is created. Execution is not evidence that delivery and payment have finished.
    Record
    Execution report and confirmation; allocation / affirmation records where applicable.
    Proof
    Match instrument, quantity, price, parties and intended settlement date. The standard T+1 rule has exceptions.
    Crypto
    A token transfer facility does not establish a trading venue, broker mandate or execution receipt.
    Status
    unproven
    Gap
    End-to-end execution is not supplied by this tokenization letter.
    Needed
    Link the actual venue and execution record to the later token movement.
    Sources: SEC: settlement-cycle rule and exceptions · NSCC CNS service · DTC tokenization no-action letter (2025-12-11)

    Step 3: Clear and prepare resourcesDependency

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    For eligible accepted CNS trades, NSCC becomes the central counterparty and nets positions by security and member. Members supply required resources.
    Actors
    NSCC; clearing members; funding providers.
    Right
    Member obligations to the CCP replace the covered bilateral obligations under the applicable rules. This is a different relationship from the customer account.
    Record
    CNS positions and member risk / funding records.
    Proof
    Establish acceptance, the applicable guarantee point, net obligations and required resources.
    Crypto
    Token movement does not by itself provide CNS novation, margin or a default guarantee.
    Status
    dependency
    Gap
    Risk-bearing capacity remains a separate service.
    Needed
    Identify any clearing arrangement or document that the trade is bilateral and how its risks are handled.
    Sources: NSCC CNS service · DTC tokenization no-action letter (2025-12-11)

    Step 4: Deliver securities and settle cashOutside scope

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    DTC processes participant securities movements; money obligations follow its settlement arrangements and settling-bank rules.
    Actors
    DTC participants; DTC; NSCC where used; settling banks.
    Right
    Securities entitlements and payment obligations change at their applicable rule-defined events. A securities entry alone does not prove all cash obligations discharged.
    Record
    DTC securities positions; money-settlement and bank records.
    Proof
    Obtain both legs, account identities and the applicable finality provisions.
    Crypto
    The letter describes token entitlement transfers without a DTC-run value leg, and contemplates any associated DvP away from DTC. It supplies no receipt for such a cash arrangement.
    Status
    outside scope
    Gap
    An integrated DTC token cash leg is outside the reviewed architecture.
    Needed
    Name the external cash asset, operator, funding and enforceable linkage between the two legs.
    Sources: DTC rules; Title VIII functional route. · NSCC CNS service · DTC tokenization no-action letter (2025-12-11)

    Step 5: Credit the holder’s recordDocumented

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    The broker maintains the customer holding; DTC maintains participant entitlements; the issuer register can continue to name Cede.
    Actors
    Broker; DTC participant; DTC; issuer / transfer agent.
    Right
    The customer’s entitlement is assessed at its own intermediary tier. New York §8-501 gives acquisition conditions, including book-entry credit; it need not wait for that intermediary to obtain the asset.
    Record
    Customer securities account → participant account → issuer register.
    Proof
    Reconcile each tier. Do not treat a retail account statement as an entry in the issuer register.
    Crypto
    LedgerScan is the official DTC record for tokenized entitlements in the reviewed design; Cede stays registered holder.
    Status
    documented
    Gap
    The record function is specified; each customer’s downstream record still needs reconciliation.
    Needed
    Obtain a matched token, LedgerScan and customer-account example for the named arrangement.
    Sources: SEC / FINRA: how securities are held (2023-07-12) · New York UCC 8-501: acquiring a security entitlement · DTC tokenization no-action letter (2025-12-11)

    Step 6: Exercise rights, exit or resolve a problemDependency

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when buying a broker-held security?
    Action
    Intermediaries handle distributions and valid entitlement orders. Sale, transfer and a failure claim follow different procedures.

    Holder; broker; issuer / agent; relevant court or receiver on failure.
    Right
    Rights to distributions and compliance with qualifying orders depend on law and agreement. A market-value loss is not automatically a compensable custody failure.
    Record
    Distribution records, entitlement orders, account terms and any claims proceeding.
    Proof
    Identify who must act, the conditions, deadline and available remedy.
    Crypto
    DTC retains correction and conversion controls in the reviewed token design. Immutability does not remove that authority.
    Status
    dependency

    Legal servicing and remedies continue alongside the token.
    Needed
    Recover current correction terms and holder-level recovery rights; do not infer a payout from a token balance.

    • Fund ↔ transfer agent / registrar: delegated recordkeeping

    Make a dollar payment

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    Baseline
    A bank-to-bank dollar transfer using Fedwire Funds
    Overlay
    USDC transfer and redemption
    Scope
    Compare outcomes, not identical instruments: a bank deposit and USDC have different obligors and terms. This Fedwire example is not a universal route for ACH, card payments, internal bank transfers or every retail transfer. Regulation J has scope exclusions. New York Article 4-A supplies a scoped rights example; its applicability is not presumed for every transfer.
    Clock
    OC 6 effective January 5, 2026; Regulation J and Circle terms checked September 10. Contractual rights are distinct from a receipt for a specific payment.
    Chain
    • Payer ↔ payer bank: deposit and instruction relationship
    • Sending bank ↔ Reserve Bank service: covered payment order
    • Beneficiary bank ↔ beneficiary: receiving account obligation
    • USDC alternative: holder ↔ applicable issuer / intermediary
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Step 1: Identify what the payer holdsDependency

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    Action

    Right
    A bank-account claim and the obligation being paid are different relationships.
    Record
    Account terms and the contract or invoice being paid.
    Proof
    Name the debtor, creditor, currency and acceptable means of payment.
    Crypto
    USDC is a separate issuer-linked asset; its terms are not bank-deposit terms.
    Status
    dependency
    Gap
    Changing the payment asset changes the claim being held.
    Needed
    Confirm that the recipient agrees to accept USDC and on what discharge terms.

    Right
    An instruction may be rejected; sending it is not the same as acceptance or completed payment.
    Record
    Authenticated order, acceptance / rejection and account identifiers.
    Proof
    Verify authorized sender, recipient and the order’s processing state.
    Crypto
    A wallet signature authorizes a token instruction under its controls; it is not a bank payment order.
    Status
    documented
    Gap
    Token instruction is a different mechanism.
    Needed
    Check custody, signing authority, correct token contract and recipient network.
    Sources: 010526 operating circular 6 · USDC Terms (2026-09-01)

    A payment message does not supply spendable funds or unlimited credit.

    Identify funding amount, availability and any credit conditions.

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    Action
    Reserve Banks process the covered order under Regulation J and OC 6.

    Service-level payment and finality follow the applicable rules; customer payout is a separate evidence point.
    Record
    Processed order and relevant service/account records.

    Identify the exact event that establishes payment under the service rules.

    Step 5: Establish what the recipient receivedDependency

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    Action
    Trace the receiving bank’s obligation and customer-account treatment under applicable law and terms.
    Actors
    Beneficiary bank; beneficiary; original payer.
    Right
    Where New York Article 4-A applies, §4-A-404 generally obliges an accepting beneficiary bank to pay the beneficiary. Section 4-A-406 links payment by the originator to bank acceptance and addresses underlying-debt discharge, subject to its conditions and exceptions. Actual customer availability is a separate fact.

    Adds a tokenized form of the DTC participant entitlement and its record. Trading, risk resources, the cash leg and customer records still need their own arrangements.

    Customer entitlements may arise before the intermediary receives the asset. Securities delivery and money settlement have separate completion events.

    Illustrative eligible CNS/DTC route. Seller-side detail and intermediary chains are summarized. The issuer register remains continuing context.

    Tokenized form · DTC

    Apply, Fund, Issue & record, Transfer / service, Redeem & pay
    Lanes
    Investor, Issuer / manager, Transfer agent, Custodian / banks, Shareholder register, Recipient / investor
    Overlay name
    BUIDL / Securitize
    Footprint
    Adds digital representations and transfer services around a fund issue. The issuer, registrar, eligibility conditions, custodian and payment obligations remain.
    Timing
    Issuance depends on the issue terms and funding confirmation. Transfer and redemption are later branches, not mandatory steps after every subscription.
    Boundary
    The filed BUIDL agreement is dated March 14, 2024. Current offering terms and later amendments are not all supplied; contract scope does not prove a completed subscription.
    Overlay lanes
    Digital form · BUIDL
    Sources: BUIDL platform, transfer agent and registrar agreement (2024-03-14) · BUIDL Solana launch and seven-network availability (2025-03-25)

    Make a dollar payment

    Home checked through: 2026-09-10 · Also shown on: What changes hands, rights and records when making a dollar payment?
    Subtitle
    From bank instruction to the recipient’s claim
    Scope
    A bank-to-bank dollar payment using Fedwire Funds. USDC is a comparison involving a different asset and obligor, not a required part of Fedwire.
    Phases
    Define the payment, Authorize, Fund & process, Receive, Use / investigate
    Lanes
    Payer, Sending bank, Reserve Bank service, Receiving bank, Beneficiary, Underlying obligation
    Overlay name
    USDC / Circle
    Footprint
    USDC supplies a transferable token claim. Issuer redemption eligibility, intermediary claims, bank payout and the original debt’s discharge remain separate questions.
    Timing
    Bank acceptance, service payment, customer availability and debt discharge are distinct events. Regulation J has scope exclusions; New York Article 4-A is a scoped rights example.
    Boundary
    OC 6 effective January 5, 2026 and Circle terms checked September 10. Not a universal ACH, card, retail or cross-border payment model.
    Overlay lanes
    USDC comparison
    Sources: USDC Terms (2026-09-01)

    USDC mint → transport → redemption

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: Circle Mint, Circle, USDC, Circle CCTP, Circle Gateway, Arc
    Objects on the path
    • Circle Mint
    • Circle Internet Financial, LLC
    • USDC reserves
    • USD Coin
    • Circle CCTP
    • Circle Gateway
    • Arc
    Links on the path
    • Circle Mint → Circle Internet Financial, LLC: institutional access
    • Circle Internet Financial, LLC → USDC reserves: segregated backing
    • Circle Internet Financial, LLC → USD Coin: non-EEA issue and redeem
    • Circle CCTP → USD Coin: native burn and mint
    • Circle Gateway → USD Coin: unified balance access
    • USD Coin → Arc: native gas and settlement asset
    Process records used
    stb-circle-mint-access-eligibility, stb-circle-mint-access, stb-circle-issuer-liability, stb-circle-mint-access-issuance, stb-circle-reserves, stb-circle-transport, stb-circle-transport-gateway, stb-circle-arc-use, stb-circle-redemption-remedy
    Kind
    stablecoin
    Description
    Follow dollars from an eligible institution through the exact issuer, segregated reserves, native USDC, cross-chain transport and redemption.
    Boundary
    Chain finality does not guarantee direct Circle redemption eligibility; issuer terms, block controls and bank payout remain separate.
    Walkthrough
    • Eligible institution funds Circle Mint and passes KYC.
    • The applicable legal issuer receives the instruction.
    • Dollar assets enter the issuer-specific segregated reserve.
    • Native USDC is minted on the selected chain.
    • USDC moves through wallets, CCTP, Gateway or Arc.
    • Redemption burns USDC under issuer eligibility rules.
    • Reserve liquidity becomes bank USD payout.
    Mapping steps
    • Step: 1 · Status: partial · Boundary: KYC and service access mapped; bank funding instruction and posting receipt absent.
    • Step: 2 · Status: mapped
    • Step: 3 · Status: partial · Boundary: Reserve pool role mapped, not transaction-level inflow posting.
    • Step: 4 · Status: partial · Boundary: Issuer instruction mapped; selected-chain execution not specified by this generic trace.
    • Step: 5 · Status: partial · Boundary: Alternative mechanisms, not successive mandatory hops. Arc uses a distinct bounded clock.
    • Step: 6 · Status: partial · Boundary: Redemption obligation mapped; no transaction-specific burn receipt.
    • Step: 7 · Status: partial · Boundary: Bank payout completion is not represented by a separate direct-Circle payout card. Tazapay is a different route and must not fill this gap.
    Mapping note
    Stage alignment uses the existing sourced process records. Unmapped actions and alternative routes remain explicit; this is not evidence of one transaction through every object.

    stb-cash-legs-ousd-issuer, stb-cash-legs-ousd-admission, stb-cash-legs-ousd-reserves, stb-cash-legs-ousd-mint-burn, stb-cash-legs-ousd-liability-record, stb-cash-legs-ousd-access, stb-cash-legs-ousd-transport, stb-cash-legs-ousd-liquidity, stb-cash-legs-ousd-cash-payout, stb-cash-legs-ousd-redemption, stb-cash-legs-ousd-legal-finality, stb-cash-legs-ousd-remedy
    Kind
    coalition-distributed payment stablecoin
    Description
    Follow OUSD from partner admission and Bridge's issuer liability through reserves, minting, four native chain records, distributor access, redemption and downstream bank payout or remedy.
    Boundary
    This is a joined launch architecture, not proof of one transaction through every layer. Launch supply is not payment volume, chain confirmation is not bank settlement, and wallet possession is not automatic direct-redemption eligibility.
    Walkthrough
    • A business enters through an eligible Open Standard partner route; direct Bridge redemption remains separately conditioned on eligible-user status and applicable terms.
    • Bridge receives the issuer-side instruction and maintains OUSD reserve value; BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY are named reserve institutions, but their exact legal mandates and account priority are not public.
    • Bridge mints OUSD and records the issuer liability while the public dashboard reconciles aggregate circulating supply and reserve assets.
    • Native OUSD token state moves on Tempo, Solana, Base or Ethereum; those networks do not become issuer, reserve owner or bank-settlement authority.
    • Mastercard, BVNK and other partners can provide wallets, conversion, sending, receiving or settlement interfaces without inheriting Bridge's issuer obligation.
    • An eligible redemption request returns to Bridge for compliance review and token burn under the issuer terms.
    • Bank USD payout, legal discharge, correction and loss allocation remain separate endpoints; no public launch-day Mastercard customer receipt or cross-party failure waterfall closes them.
    Mapping steps
    • Step: 1 · Status: partial · Boundary: Partner access is mapped, but provider-specific contracts, eligibility, fees and production state differ.
    • Step: 2 · Status: partial · Boundary: Reserve classes and named institutions are public; exact mandates, account title, cash receipt and priority are not.
    • Step: 3 · Status: partial · Boundary: Issuer, supply and aggregate reconciliation are mapped; transaction-level incoming cash and liability posting are not.
    • Step: 4 · Status: mapped · Boundary: Four native deployments and launch supply are mapped; a common cross-chain finality and recovery mechanism is not.
    • Step: 5 · Status: partial · Boundary: Advertised and named routes are mapped; no named Mastercard production customer or route volume is public.
    • Step: 6 · Status: partial · Boundary: Issuer terms establish the obligation and controls; no launch-day stress redemption or transaction-specific burn receipt is mapped.
    • Step: 7 · Status: unrepresented · Boundary: Cash posting, legal discharge and the cross-party failure waterfall remain unresolved endpoints.
    Mapping note
    Launch-day architecture. The trace deliberately preserves issuer, governance, reserve, distributor, chain, redemption, bank-payout and remedy clocks rather than presenting a single atomic payment.

    The seven accounting layers

    · 7 rows

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/TOKENIZATION_ENTITY_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY_2026-09-01.json › accounting_layers

    1 · Who owes whom?

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    OBJECT, AUTHORITY
    Explanation
    A customer deposit is the customer’s asset and the bank’s liability. A token representation does not automatically create a second independent claim.
    Question
    Who is the issuer or debtor, and what exact right does the holder own?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    2 · Custody & access

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    ADMISSION, FUNDING
    Explanation
    Deposits, segregated custody and control of keys are different arrangements. Identify the asset holder, account provider and person authorized to move value.
    Question
    Where is the value held, who controls it and who is allowed to instruct?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    3 · Funding & inventory

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    FUNDING
    Explanation
    Funding confirmed before execution does not mean final settlement has occurred. Reservation, credit, collateral and prefunding carry different exposures.
    Question
    What balance, credit or collateral supports the payment, for how long and at whose cost?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    4 · Shared commitment

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    INSTRUCTION, EXECUTION, TECH_STATE
    Explanation
    A shared record lets relevant parties coordinate payment state. An informational record is not automatically a separate financial asset or the authoritative legal register.
    Question
    What is authorized, recorded and executed; who can see it; what makes the commitment binding?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    5 · Clearing & netting

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    CLEARING
    Explanation
    Matching agrees the obligations; netting calculates an offset amount under applicable rules. Neither alone supplies a settlement asset or guarantee.
    Question
    Are obligations matched, netted, novated or guaranteed—and by whom?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    6 · Cash & finality

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    CASH, AUTH_RECORD, FINALITY, POSTING
    Explanation
    Customer credit, technical confirmation, cash settlement and legal finality can occur at different times. Identify which books discharge the obligation.
    Question
    What asset settles the payment, which record controls and when is discharge final?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    7 · Failure & remedy

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which books record ownership, custody, operations and accounting?
    Families
    CORRECTION, DEFAULT, BACKSTOP, PROOF
    Explanation
    If the recipient can spend before banks settle and settlement fails, a contract and a balance sheet must carry the gap.
    Question
    Who can correct or reverse, who bears loss, and what stress evidence exists?
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Also shown on: Which institutions and records support conventional securities, payments and funds?
    Kind
    current stack
    Description
    How a broker-held cash equity clears and settles today: NSCC, CNS, DTC, Cede, NSS, settling banks. Overlay shows crypto attachments that do not replace those books.
    Boundary
    Solid nodes are the current machine. Overlay nodes are overlap, not overtake, unless that office’s T-account changes occupant.
    Walkthrough
    • Start with the street-name claim: the investor has an entitlement against a carrying broker, not title at the issuer.
    • Eligible broker-to-broker trades are captured in UTC and novated at NSCC. DTCC parent is not the CCP.
    • CNS nets one long or short per Member per security versus NSCC.
    • Securities move on DTC’s participant file. Cede stays the registered holder.
    • Money is not paid trade-by-trade. NSCC’s net, DTC as NSS agent, and the Fed’s NSS file debit settling banks.
    • 47 banks currently may act as DTC settling banks. Designation for a given member is not on this map.
    • Overlay: Hidden Road can sit as a DTC participant; DTC tokenization can re-represent the participant entitlement. Neither rewrites Cede or NSS.

    • USDC is a Circle liability with reserve custody at BNY for the Circle Reserve Fund — a different claim.

    Securitize infrastructure anatomy

    Cutoff: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Who performs each step of a Securitize product?
    Still being checked
    • Obtain or observe a public FINRA/BrokerCheck description that directly reflects the reported 2026 custody, underwriting and selling-group expansion.
    • Track production evidence and volumes for the NYSE digital-platform, Computershare and Continental relationships rather than treating partnership announcements as completed market migration.
    • Track BRSRV assets, supported chains, stablecoin-issuer use and network-outage or correction evidence separately from its launch.
    • Track the EU TSS opening, admitted instruments, members, settlement asset and production volumes separately from CNMV authorization.
    • Resolve product by product whether the official register is an off-chain control book, a composite blockchain-plus-identity register, or a linked incumbent register.
    Cutoff
    2026-09-17 ET
    Summary
    Securitize is best understood as a regulated securities-control plane rather than a blockchain or a general crypto-finance conglomerate. Its group joins transfer agency, broker-dealer and ATS functions, investment advice, fund administration, tokenization software and an EU trading-and-settlement venue while relying on outside issuers, asset managers, custodians, public networks and cash rails.
    Boundary
    Group consolidation does not merge the licenses, appointments or duties of the named subsidiaries. A token can be part of an official shareholder register in one product, a representation reconciled to a transfer-agent control book in another, or a secondary layer attached to an incumbent registrar in a third.
    Thesis
    The strategic asset is not a coin. It is the ability to keep the legal security, investor identity, transfer restrictions, official record, corporate actions, trading access and correction powers joined across several technical ledgers.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Who performs each step of a Securitize product?

    Boundary
    A public wallet address alone is not a verified shareholder identity or permission to hold every product.

    Product-specific official register: control book, composite blockchain-plus-identity register, or linked incumbent register

    Ripple and Securitize: two different control planes

    · 11 rows

    Ripple and Securitize: two different control planes

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Entity: Ripple · Also shown on: How do Ripple and Securitize divide the jobs of a money and securities business?
    Thesis
    Ripple organizes the movement, custody, liquidity and enterprise management of money and digital assets. Securitize organizes the creation, ownership, transfer, servicing and correction of regulated securities. Their strongest fit is not duplication but a title-side and cash-side interface.
    Boundary
    The two groups can meet in one transaction without merging their authorities. Ripple does not become the issuer or transfer agent for a fund share; Securitize does not become the issuer of RLUSD, a cross-border payment network, a prime broker for all assets or a corporate treasury-management system.
    Interface
    • Title: Where they actually meet: BUIDL or VBILL to RLUSD
    • Steps: An eligible investor begins with a fund-share claim recorded and transfer-restricted through the Securitize-controlled product process., The enabled smart-contract functionality allows eligible BUIDL or VBILL shares to be exchanged to Ripple for RLUSD; the public announcement does not expose every intermediary book, price, mint/burn or bank-cash entry., The fund-share position must be cancelled, transferred or otherwise reconciled on the applicable shareholder record. A wallet transfer alone is not proof that this legal step completed., RLUSD is delivered as a separate stablecoin claim governed by its issuer and token terms. It is not the same asset or record as the redeemed fund share., Bank cash enters only if the holder later redeems or off-ramps RLUSD through an eligible route; neither announcement nor token delivery proves that bank payout occurred.
    • Proof state: The September 2025 release establishes an enabled RLUSD exchange option and planned additional integration. It does not publish route volume, a full accounting waterfall, universal XRPL use or evidence that Ripple controls Securitize's shareholder records.
    Watch
    • Route-level volume and accounting receipts for BUIDL or VBILL exchanges into RLUSD.
    • Whether Securitize Markets' reported atomic stablecoin settlement uses RLUSD, another stablecoin or several settlement assets in production.
    • A named product in which Ripple Custody, Ripple Prime or Ripple Treasury is operationally joined to Securitize's issuance and transfer-agent stack.
    • Production evidence for the announced XRPL integration, including which security, which authoritative record and which correction process applies.
    • Any ownership, acquisition or exclusive-control change; partnership and technical integration do not establish corporate control.
    Sources: Ripple cross-border payments product (2026-09-01) · Securitize July 2026 S-1 (2026-07-31) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31) · Ripple closes Standard Custody acquisition (2024-06-11) · Ripple–Securitize RLUSD functionality (2025-09-23) · Ripple Custody product (2026-09-01) · Securitize and Computershare tokenized-shares agreement (2026-04-29) · Securitize Q2 2026 results and operating update (2026-08-12) · Ripple launches U.S. digital-asset spot prime brokerage (2026) · FINRA BrokerCheck report for Securitize Markets, LLC (2026-09-17) · Ripple Treasury launch (2026) · Securitize Q2 2026 MD&A (2026-08-13) · Wormhole XRPL integration announcement (2025-06-26) · BUIDL Solana launch and seven-network availability (2025-03-25) · CNMV approval of the SECURITIZE DLT TSS (2025-11-26) · Ripple National Trust Bank preliminary conditional approval (2025-12-12) · Securitize Corp. current subsidiary list (2026-07-08) · BUIDL platform, transfer agent and registrar agreement (2024-03-14)

    Distinction
    Ripple is route-centered; Securitize is instrument-and-title-centered.

    Securitize
    The outside issuer or fund creates the security; Securitize records and services it when appointed. Securitize has no universal house stablecoin or money claim.
    Distinction
    Ripple owns a money-issuance seat; Securitize usually owns a service-and-record seat around someone else's security.

    Securitize
    The appointed transfer agent can maintain the controlling shareholder record: an off-chain control book, a blockchain-plus-identity composite register or a layer linked to an incumbent registrar.

    Securitize

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: How do Ripple and Securitize divide the jobs of a money and securities business?
    Ripple
    Product contracts, issuer records, custody controls, market books and payment rails determine reversal, asset return and cash remedy. Ripple cannot correct an outside fund's shareholder register merely by moving RLUSD or recording an XRPL transaction.
    Securitize
    When appointed, the transfer agent can freeze, claw back, burn, reissue and correct the current shareholder record; it cannot by that authority compel a bank payout or rewrite an outside stablecoin issuer's liability.
    Distinction
    Ripple repairs the money, custody or market leg under the relevant product; Securitize repairs the security-title leg under the governing instrument.

    Where Ripple and Securitize fit into the GENIUS Act

    Where Ripple and Securitize fit into the GENIUS Act

    Cutoff: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Cutoff
    2026-09-17
    Status
    Enacted statute; core implementation remains proposed at this cutoff
    Thesis
    GENIUS supplies the federal constitution for the payment-stablecoin cash leg. It reaches Ripple directly through RLUSD and Standard Custody's issuer obligation. It reaches Securitize mainly when a regulated security is funded, exchanged, settled, custodied or redeemed through a payment stablecoin.
    Boundary
    GENIUS does not turn a tokenized fund share into money, authorize the underlying security, approve a blockchain, or merge the stablecoin issuer's ledger with the transfer agent's shareholder record. A named charter, current state approval or product integration is not by itself a GENIUS permitted-payment-stablecoin-issuer approval.
    Interface
    • Title: One transaction, two regimes
    • Steps: The investor holds a security whose eligibility, title, transfer restrictions and servicing are governed by securities law, product documents and the appointed recordkeeper., Securitize validates the investor and reconciles the security-side instruction; the fund share must be cancelled, transferred or otherwise reflected on the authoritative shareholder record., RLUSD is delivered as a distinct payment-stablecoin claim against its issuing entity. GENIUS governs the issuer, reserves, redemption, compliance and holder-priority architecture once operative., If the holder later redeems RLUSD, the issuer-side process extinguishes or reconciles the token claim and pays eligible bank cash under the applicable terms. That bank-cash receipt is another record, not automatic proof from the on-chain transfer alone.
    • Reading: GENIUS standardizes the money object at the handoff. It does not standardize the security, replace Securitize's shareholder record or prove that every announced exchange completed all accounting and cash-settlement steps.
    Watch
    • A final OCC or other primary-regulator implementing rule and the resulting 120-day effective-date calculation.
    • Certification of New York's regime and a public approval naming Standard Custody, Ripple National Trust Bank or another exact entity as a permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
    • Any product-level evidence that a Securitize-administered fund or tokenized instrument is actually held as an RLUSD reserve asset, rather than merely being exchangeable into RLUSD.
    • The exact Securitize affiliate and stablecoin used in production atomic settlement, including customer, custody, order-control and accounting records.
    • Final customer-identification, BSA, sanctions and lawful-order rules, plus actual implementation across the named issuer and service-provider entities.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · OCC GENIUS Act implementation proposal (2026-02-25) · Permitted payment stablecoin issuer customer-identification proposal (2026-06-22) · Treasury GENIUS issuance, offer and sale proposal (2026-08-18) · OCC statement targeting a GENIUS final rule by November (2026-08-19) · RLUSD reserve transparency and issuer description (2026-09-03) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31) · Ripple National Trust Bank preliminary conditional approval (2025-12-12) · Securitize July 2026 S-1 (2026-07-31) · Ripple–Securitize RLUSD functionality (2025-09-23) · Ripple cross-border payments product (2026-09-01) · Securitize Q2 2026 results and operating update (2026-08-12)

    Statute enacted

    Meaning
    Public Law 119-27 is enacted. Enactment and general operational effectiveness are separate clocks.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18)

    Implementation at cutoff

    Date: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Date
    2026-09-17
    State
    proposed
    Meaning
    The located OCC, joint customer-identification and Treasury section 3 actions are proposals. Treasury's section 3 comment period runs to October 19; the OCC publicly targeted a final rule by November, but a target is not a final rule.
    Sources: OCC GENIUS Act implementation proposal (2026-02-25) · Permitted payment stablecoin issuer customer-identification proposal (2026-06-22) · Treasury GENIUS issuance, offer and sale proposal (2026-08-18) · OCC statement targeting a GENIUS final rule by November (2026-08-19)

    General effective date

    Date: 2027-01-18 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Date
    2027-01-18 or earlier trigger
    State
    future
    Meaning
    The Act generally becomes effective on the earlier of January 18, 2027 or 120 days after the primary federal payment-stablecoin regulators issue final implementing regulations.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · OCC GENIUS Act implementation proposal (2026-02-25)

    Provider asset gate

    Date: 2028-07-18 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Date
    2028-07-18
    State
    future
    Meaning
    Beginning three years after enactment, a covered U.S. digital-asset service provider generally may offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a U.S. person only if the coin is issued by a permitted issuer, subject to the statutory exceptions and foreign route.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · Treasury GENIUS issuance, offer and sale proposal (2026-08-18)

    Which object is inside GENIUS?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    RLUSD fits the payment-stablecoin definition because it is designed for payment or settlement and carries a fixed-dollar redemption obligation. XRP does not fit that definition merely because it can move value: it has no issuer obligation to redeem at a fixed monetary value.
    Securitize
    BUIDL, VBILL, BRSRV/RSVXX and tokenized public-equity interests remain securities. The Act's definition excludes securities from payment stablecoins, even when the security has a dollar NAV or can be exchanged into a stablecoin.
    Effect
    GENIUS governs the RLUSD cash claim; securities law and the governing instrument continue to govern the fund share or equity claim.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · RLUSD reserve transparency and issuer description (2026-09-03) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31)

    Who must pass the issuer gate?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    Standard Custody & Trust Company is the disclosed RLUSD issuer and current NYDFS-chartered obligor. To issue under the federal regime it must fit an approved state-qualified or federal-qualified route. Ripple's brand, software licenses and preliminary national trust-bank approval do not substitute for approval of the exact issuing entity.
    Securitize
    Securitize is generally transfer agent, broker-dealer/ATS, adviser, administrator or technology provider around securities issued by outside funds and companies. It does not become the RLUSD issuer by offering the exchange interface.
    Effect
    The entity owing the dollar redemption is the regulated center of the GENIUS analysis, not the chain, wallet, transfer agent or brand alone.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · RLUSD reserve transparency and issuer description (2026-09-03) · Ripple National Trust Bank preliminary conditional approval (2025-12-12) · Securitize July 2026 S-1 (2026-07-31)

    What backs the cash leg?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    A permitted issuer must maintain identifiable reserves at least one-for-one in the statutory categories and meet redemption, disclosure, custody and supervisory requirements. RLUSD's disclosed short-duration reserve design is directionally aligned, but regulator approval and exact final-rule conformance remain separate findings.
    Securitize
    A tokenized Treasury or fund share is not automatically an eligible RLUSD reserve asset. The statute can admit a registered government money-market fund invested solely in eligible assets and tokenized versions of permitted reserves, but actual eligibility depends on the exact product, portfolio, legal ownership and regulator treatment.
    Effect
    BUIDL or BRSRV proximity to Treasuries does not prove that Standard Custody holds that instrument in RLUSD reserves. A product receipt is required.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · RLUSD reserve transparency and issuer description (2026-09-03) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31)

    Where can yield sit?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    GENIUS bars a permitted or qualifying foreign issuer from paying interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the payment stablecoin.
    Securitize
    A separately constituted fund share can carry investment return because it is a security rather than the payment stablecoin. Exchanging RLUSD for a security, or a security for RLUSD, preserves two instruments and two claims.
    Effect
    Securitize can form a yield-bearing investment layer adjacent to a non-yielding stablecoin cash layer, but that is a legal separation—not evidence of an exemption, evasion route or automatic product approval.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31) · Ripple–Securitize RLUSD functionality (2025-09-23)

    Who can freeze or correct what?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    The stablecoin issuer must have the technical capability to comply with lawful orders that can require seizure, freezing, burning or prevention of transfer of identified payment stablecoins or accounts. BSA, sanctions, customer-identification and due-diligence duties also attach to the issuer framework.
    Securitize
    An appointed transfer agent can freeze, claw back, burn, reissue or correct the security-side shareholder record under the governing instrument. That authority does not let it rewrite Standard Custody's stablecoin liability.
    Effect
    Stablecoin control and security-title correction are separate remedy systems even when one interface coordinates them.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · Permitted payment stablecoin issuer customer-identification proposal (2026-06-22) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31)

    How do the operating companies enter?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    Ripple Payments, Custody, Prime, Treasury or distribution entities can enter the analysis when an exact entity exchanges, transfers, safeguards, offers or sells a payment stablecoin for compensation. Their other products are not converted into stablecoin issuance merely because RLUSD is available inside the stack.
    Securitize
    Securitize Markets or another exact affiliate can enter as a digital-asset service provider on the stablecoin funding, exchange, settlement or custody leg. The securities placement, ATS, transfer-agency and fund-administration legs retain their separate legal bases.
    Effect
    The 2028 provider gate will function like an asset-eligibility rule at covered U.S. intermediaries; application turns on the exact entity, activity, customer and coin.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · Treasury GENIUS issuance, offer and sale proposal (2026-08-18) · Ripple cross-border payments product (2026-09-01) · Securitize Q2 2026 results and operating update (2026-08-12)

    What happens if one side fails?

    Home checked through: 2026-09-17 · Also shown on: Which Ripple and Securitize roles are affected by GENIUS?
    Ripple
    GENIUS creates reserve-asset and bankruptcy priorities for payment-stablecoin holders and distinguishes the issuer's redemption obligation from a wallet balance or market price.
    Securitize
    The investor's rights in the fund or equity security continue to depend on the issuer, governing documents and controlling shareholder record. A corrected share register does not itself produce dollars; a successful stablecoin redemption does not itself restore the share.
    Effect
    A failed combined transaction must be diagnosed leg by leg: security title, stablecoin delivery, stablecoin issuer claim and bank-cash payout.
    Sources: GENIUS Act — Public Law 119-27 (2025-07-18) · Ripple–Securitize RLUSD functionality (2025-09-23) · BlackRock BRSRV / RSVXX prospectus (2026-07-31)

    DTC / DTCC tokenization

    Home checked through: 2026-09-01 · Entity: Depository Trust Company
    Kind
    regulated depository + tokenized entitlement service
    Description
    Follow DTC from conditional SEC staff posture through the issuer register, participant entitlement, token conversion, official DTC record, correction controls and operating clocks.
    Boundary
    Cede, the participant entitlement, LedgerScan and the chain token are related but distinct records.
    Walkthrough
    • Start with the conditional SEC staff position, not a final rule or approval.
    • Separate DTCC parent, DTC regulated operator and DTCC Digital software roles.
    • Keep Cede as issuer-register holder and the participant account as the conventional entitlement.
    • Move the underlying into DTC’s Digital Omnibus Account before Factory minting.
    • Transfer only among registered wallets while LedgerScan maintains DTC’s official token record.
    • Preserve DTC root controls, detokenization and corporate-action correction paths.
    • End with July limited production, expected October launch and planned Stellar availability.

    The Ample-Reserves Machine Can Run Away From Its OperatorsOfficial

    Date: 2026-07-13 · Also shown on: What tokenization and clearing actions appear in the saved official record?
    Date
    2026-07-13
    Agency
    Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia
    Type
    Research
    Summary
    Working Paper 26-34, by Philadelphia EVP Roc Armenter: the 'ample' level of reserves is itself a function of liquid deposits, so reaching ample is not the same as being normalized. Feed reserves in, banks create deposits, deposits raise the ample bar, the Desk feeds more in — and at modest deposit persistence the loop goes explosive. His fix is to attenuate the Desk's response and accept small deviations between the effective funds rate and interest on reserves. Context the paper supplies: QT ended December 2025, the balance sheet is over 20 percent of nominal GDP against roughly 5 percent in 2006, and the Desk now runs Reserve Management Purchases under the April 29 2026 implementation note. A sitting Reserve Bank executive publishing that the floor system carries an unpriced instability, two weeks before the meeting.
    Tags
    ample reserves, balance sheet, Reserve Management Purchases, Armenter, floor system, EFFR
    Record kind
    official
    Sources: philadelphiafed.org

    Press Release 2026-69 announces a Sept 17, 2026 roundtable at SEC headquarters on moving toward 24-hour trading in U.S. equity markets, 'including preparations to support overnight trading, operations and resiliency in a 24-hour market,' and opens a public comment file, No. 4-913. Atkins: 'We are moving towards a new day - and night - in the U.S. equity markets.' The clearing and settlement questions of a market that never closes now have a docket to pile up in. Companion to the 24X and NSCC extended-hours track.
    Tags
    SEC, 24-hour trading, File 4-913, Atkins, overnight settlement
    Record kind
    official
    Sources: sec.gov

    SEC order approving a CME Securities Clearing Inc. proposed rule change supporting members' risk management and their ability to authorize persons as Users.     A Clearing House for Bets on Earnings — Cboe Clear's Amended ApplicationOfficial

    Date: 2026-07-24 · Also shown on: What tokenization and clearing actions appear in the saved official record?
    Date
    2026-07-24
    Agency
    SEC
    Type
    Application
    Summary
    SEC notice of filing of an amended application by Cboe Clear U.S. for temporary registration as a clearing agency under Section 17A. FR Doc. 2026-14979, 91 FR 46817-46821, published Jul 24. CCUS would clear 'cash settled, binary security options, including among others, security options overlying key performance indicators (KPIs) reported by certain issuers of stock' — prediction-market structure walking into registered clearing. The filing also discusses digital assets and notes CCUS does not require prefunding of margin, relying on partial and full tear-ups to manage liquidity risk. Comment period open.
    Tags
    Cboe Clear, clearing agency, binary KPI options, prediction markets, tear-up
    Record kind
    official

    What is uncertain

    • Illustrative teaching entries for role discrimination. Not GAAP or IFRS policy and not a named firm’s actual journal. Named occupants are sourced legal persons or process offices for that seat. Unnamed seats are evidence gaps, not empty markets. A brand, parent, token or chain does not inherit the seat.
    • Overtake means this office’s proprietary or fiduciary books of the economic object are now someone else’s. Overlap is a different claim, a membership, or a software path hanging off the same rail.
    • Technical finality, authoritative legal record and cash or redemption remedy are separate endpoints. Proposal, staff position, registration, ownership, partnership, software capability, pilot and production are different facts and clocks.
    • Group consolidation does not merge the licenses, appointments or duties of the named subsidiaries. A token can be part of an official shareholder register in one product, a representation reconciled to a transfer-agent control book in another, or a secondary layer attached to an incumbent registrar in a third.
    • The books entries are illustrative teaching entries for working out who plays which role, not any named firm's actual books.
    • crypto_companies_and_networks.json carries journal_entry_routes only as a pointer to process_walk.json; the walks above are the home.
    • The Transfer Agent Modernization package holds only a source manifest (12 sources) and a README; there is no provision-level registry, so the proposal is read through the Crypto Hub's SEC-proposal nodes.
